A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedVTC work despite the changed title and conference formatting. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison; the conflicting settings in v2 are document inconsistencies rather than missing evidence.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original federated-learning simulations on four datasets, including accuracy, communication costs, memory requirements and ablations. Appendix B includes experimental settings and accuracy curves.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds pFedAFM comparisons and MNIST hyperparameter-sensitivity results in Appendix B.4 and Figure 8.

M1.justification: The VTC architecture, Gaussian reparameterization, ELBO and distribution-matching losses, alternating training, aggregation and fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. The revised synthetic-sample count concerns the reported experimental budget.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST, CIFAR10, CIFAR100 and Tiny-ImageNet under Dirichlet parameters 0.1 and 1.0. The new sensitivity studies use existing MNIST coverage; no additional dataset, task or population is evaluated.

E2.justification: pFedAFM is added to the accuracy and communication comparisons in Tables 1–2 and the memory comparison in Figure 3. All five earlier baselines remain; Figure 7 retains its original comparator set.

E3.justification: Section 3.4 changes S/C samples per class, totaling S, to S per class, totaling S×C: a substantial reported fine-tuning-budget revision. However, Algorithm 1 still specifies S total samples, and v2's Section 4.1 and Appendix B.4 disagree on CIFAR10's S value, 500 versus 1000. Actual budgets or rerunning are therefore unestablished. v2 also introduces MNIST S and lambda sweeps.

E4.justification: Appendix B.4 and Figure 8 add sensitivity analyses of synthetic-sample count and distribution-matching weight on MNIST Dirichlet(1.0). The transmission-frequency and loss ablations remain unchanged. Table 7 summarizes the fine-tuning transition already plotted in Figure 7.

E5.justification: Both versions report three independent trials and mean ± standard deviation in Table 1. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: All pre-existing numerical entries in Tables 1–4 and the Figure 7 curves are retained. v2 adds pFedAFM outcomes, including 87.2±0.4% on MNIST Dirichlet(1.0), and Figure 8 sensitivity results. Table 7 explicitly quantifies the retained fine-tuning transitions as gains of 3.3–10.1 percentage points.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same objective, Gaussian assumptions, KL expression and loss derivations. Appendix A's model-heterogeneity definitions are preserved. No theorem, proof or substantive mathematical correction is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain synthetic-data fine-tuning for heterogeneous clients without a public training dataset, ELBO-plus-distribution-matching training, and improved accuracy with communication and memory efficiency. Retitling and shortening the conclusion do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B.5 newly explains why downstream training utility, rather than visual realism or FID, measures synthetic-sample quality. Appendix B.4 interprets excessive samples as potentially redundant. The broader-impact assertions about data shortage and Byzantine/model-inversion protection are removed, while the computation-cost limitation and future directions remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B.4 newly documents hyperparameter tuning and supplies empirical support for lambda=0.1, previously justified by following prior work. Its sample-count disclosures introduce inconsistencies with the main text and algorithm. Hardware, software and the detailed VTC architectures in Table 6 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: A new Section 2.3 discusses federated diffusion, GAN and CLIP approaches and their resource requirements. v2 also adds pFedGen discussion and pFedAFM/FID references, while removing the model-inversion reference accompanying the deleted broader-impact paragraph. The existing research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, rewrites the abstract, standardizes much TC terminology to VTC, condenses the conclusion and swaps the architecture and accuracy-curve appendix subsections. Acknowledgements and an LLM-use disclosure are added. Most existing methodological and experimental prose remains.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 receive revised arrows, legends and annotations; Tables 1–2 and Figure 3 accommodate pFedAFM. Figure 8 and Table 7 are added. Conference formatting, table styling, placement and captions change, while the existing Figure 4 examples and Figure 7 plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The added baseline, sensitivity evidence and synthetic-quality explanation provide useful improvements. However, v1's consistent total-S description becomes conflicting total/per-class counts in v2, alongside conflicting CIFAR10 defaults. These discrepancies impede reproduction and assessment of comparison fairness for the retained primary results. Their significance relative to the added evidence prevents a reliable net quality judgment.
